brief: GS TMT sales note covering several threads. TSMC hit an all-time high after Elon Musk confirmed preliminary talks on a TSMC role in Terafab's Texas chip project (~$16.8bn initial investment, $55-119bn total spend); a partnership could cut execution risk but complicate Intel's role, with no agreement reached and TSMC's October 15 call next. GS's Q3 semiconductor preview is constructive after the SOX's 11% two-month pullback, arguing expectations are now more achievable; it favors SemiCap, compute, analog and memory/storage, preferring AMAT, STX and MCHP into earnings over QCOM, KLAC and WDC, while SIA data show shipments ~10% above trend, benefiting Microchip, NXP and Analog Devices most. Schneider Electric's $23.7bn all-cash deal for PTC at $205/share validates industrial-software valuations and pressures Dassault Systèmes, though DSY keeps its simulation differentiation and is hard to acquire given the Dassault family's ~40% control. Goldman upgrades Stagwell to Buy ($13 target) and initiates Havas at Neutral (€19). Hedge fund net leverage fell toward five-year lows as Europe saw its largest net buying in five years, and hyperscaler debt issuance is seen rising to $420bn by 2027, pressuring long-end yields higher.
